passage:
At the beginning of the year, each student received a new notebook for writing practice. Most students filled the first page carefully.
Jack did not. He stared at the empty page for a long time because he was afraid of making mistakes.
His teacher noticed and wrote one sentence at the top: "This notebook is for practice, not perfection."
Jack smiled and began writing.
By the end of the semester, his notebook had messy pages, crossed-out words, drawings, and many corrections. It was not beautiful, but it showed progress.
Jack learned that an empty page may look clean, but it cannot teach much. A used page, even a messy one, can show that learning happened.
